PullRequest.Title: Rerun failed browser unit tests in fresh browsers
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Add bounded retries for browser unit-test failures, matching the fresh-process/window retry behavior of the Node and Electron runners.

### Changes

- Add `--rerun-failed-files <count>` to rerun failed tests and failed-hook suites in a freshly launched browser. Fall back to whole test files when title selection is unsuitable.
- Track failures separately for each browser and require an actual pass in the same test file before clearing a failure. Skipped or renamed tests and attempts with unattributed failures cannot turn the run green.
- Keep per-attempt CI results and report recovered failures as flaky tests. Disable retries when debugging.
- Enable two reruns in the macOS, Linux, and Windows pull request workflows, increase the Windows browser-test timeout to 25 minutes, and document the behavior.

### Validation

- `node --check test/unit/browser/index.js` — passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --help` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- test/unit/browser/index.js` — passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --browser webkit --sequential --run src/vs/base/test/common/arrays.test.ts --grep '^Arrays' --rerun-failed-files 2 --reporter dot` — passed: 29 tests in Chromium and 29 in WebKit on macOS.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit-time hygiene hook — passed.

Windows and the full CI/browser suites were not run locally. No regression-test file is included in this six-file change.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed control flow, unbounded target cardinality after the explicit >50 fallback, and nested full-result scans are directly visible. Exact wall-clock cost varies with failure prevalence and suite size, but the repeated-work mechanism and its placement after every rerun on the critical path are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and short-lived arrays/JSON strings while filtering and serializing test title paths
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For T outstanding targets, P passes, and F failures in a rerun, findPassedTargets performs O(T*(P+F)) scans; above MAX_RERUN_TARGETS the whole-file fallback leaves T unbounded, so a broad failure can make this quadratic in the number of tests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased rerun latency and CPU/GC pressure on the CI critical path, potentially consuming much of the browser-test timeout after a large rerun has already completed
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR the browser runner executed one attempt and did not reconcile failed targets against a later attempt, so this repeated result-scanning work did not exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new retry loop calls findPassedTargets after each rerun; for every outstanding target, the added lines refilter all failures and all passes and repeatedly JSON-stringify title paths.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 757 places `result.failures.filter(...)` inside `[...targets].filter(...)`; adjacent added line 760 likewise filters all `result.passed` for every target. The new whole-file fallback at added lines 731-734 allows the enclosing target map to exceed 50.
Findings.Title: Index rerun results before reconciling failed targets
Findings.Impact: When an infrastructure or shared-state failure produces more than 50 failed browser tests and a fresh-browser attempt recovers, the whole-file rerun can return thousands of passes while hundreds or thousands of targets remain. Reconciliation then repeatedly scans that complete result set once per target, delaying CI completion even though the browser work has finished.
Findings.Evidence: planRerun switches to whole-file mode when targets.size exceeds 50 but preserves every target in the map. runTestsWithReruns then passes that unbounded map to findPassedTargets. At lines 757-760, each target runs result.failures.filter, constructs a failed-path Set, runs result.passed.filter with JSON.stringify per pass, and then searches those arrays again. Thus 1,000 targets and 5,000 rerun passes cause roughly five million pass inspections plus allocations and stringification, rather than one indexing pass.
Findings.Recommendation: Build per-file indexes of failures and non-ambiguous passes once per attempt, including precomputed serialized title-path keys, then resolve all targets from those indexes in O(P+F+T). Preserve the existing file/test/suite matching and teardown-failure semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal successful PR browser-unit run (Chromium on Linux/Windows or WebKit on macOS)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host globs test modules, starts one local HTTP server, launches one Playwright browser, creates a context/page, globs and compresses CSS metadata, loads the renderer over localhost, imports all selected modules sequentially, runs Mocha, writes reporter output, then closes the browser. The diff's retry loop returns immediately after the first successful attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob all test modules under the compiled output tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One glob per runner invocation, producing the browser-compatible module list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before any browser can launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch and close a Playwright browser process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch for the single browser used by each PR job when tests pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One launch and close per configured browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Browser startup and shutdown are on the test job critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob CSS files and optionally read localization messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One CSS glob per browser attempt; one localization read only with `--build`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations once per browser run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before tests execute in the page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve renderer/static modules over a localhost HTTP server and import selected test modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server per browser attempt; one dynamic import per selected module plus static dependency requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same local server and module-loading path for the single attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All selected module loads must complete before Mocha runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send Mocha events from the browser page to Node through `page.exposeFunction`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several events per test/hook plus suite events; unchanged event count, with added retry metadata in payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event calls occurred without the added file/type/path/ambiguity fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event serialization/dispatch occurs during the test run, but added payload work is linear and small relative to the existing event stream.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One result file for the successful first attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One result file with the same base path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter finalization is part of run completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All browser-compatible test modules selected by the default `**/*.test.js` glob and all tests/suites registered by those modules.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each PR workflow invokes one browser, so effective browser concurrency is one. The local default can run three browser types concurrently as before; the diff does not add concurrency within one browser's attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-attempt browser cache is retained because each attempt launches a fresh browser. Module discovery is computed once in the host; CSS glob/compression and browser page/module loading occur once on a successful run. There is no retry-result cache on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced boundaries and early-return behavior; no reportable normal-success regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of tests and added bytes per event varies with the built tree, but the normal-run diff overhead is bounded linear traversal/allocation and does not establish a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The normal path still performs one browser attempt; added duplicate-path bookkeeping and pass-result retention are linear and not independently shown to cause meaningful latency or memory pressure.

Scenarios.Scenario: One to fifty attributable test or suite failures with retries enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the first failed attempt closes its browser, the host plans a title-targeted rerun, starts a fresh server/browser, loads only unique files containing outstanding targets, selects matching tests in the renderer, runs them, and may repeat once more in PR CI. Each attempt must complete before the next begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a fresh Playwright browser for each retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two additional launches per configured browser in PR CI, only after attributable failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The job stopped after the first failed browser attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each launch is serial and directly extends failed/flaky test-job latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat CSS glob/compression and create per-attempt JUnit XML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per retry attempt; at most two extra operations/files per PR browser job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These operations occurred only for the original attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CSS discovery/compression precedes each rerun; reporter output completes with each attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a fresh localhost server and reload renderer plus failed test files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server/page load per retry; imports are grouped by unique failed file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No second server/page/module load after failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to provide the intended clean-browser retry isolation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transmit Mocha events and retry result metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Proportional to tests/hooks actually selected from the unique failed files; target selection is capped at 50.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs during each rerun and supplies authoritative pass/fail evidence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 50 deduplicated test/suite targets; effective module cardinality is the number of unique files containing those targets, not the number of targets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Retries are serialized per browser. PR jobs configure one browser. Local runs may have up to three independent browser retry sequences in parallel, matching the pre-existing browser-level concurrency; no shared limiter exists, but aggregate concurrency does not exceed the configured browser count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh-browser semantics deliberately discard browser/module caches between attempts. The host reuses the original module list only to derive retry files; no in-flight attempt coalescing is needed because each browser owns one sequential retry loop. No negative cache applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that retries add expensive fresh-browser and reload boundaries, but also that they are sequential, capped, and reached only on failure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser launch and module-load durations vary by platform and failed file, but the two-retry cap and unique-file grouping make the added work bounded and intentional.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Added latency is the explicit fresh-browser retry behavior, bounded to two retries in PR CI and grouped by unique file.

Scenarios.Scenario: Broad attributable failure causing whole-file fallback, followed by a recovering rerun
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first attempt records more than 50 outstanding targets. `planRerun` loads their unique whole files in a fresh browser. After that attempt reports passes/failures, Node must reconcile every outstanding target before it can declare recovery, schedule the last retry, or finish the job. The new reconciliation repeatedly scans all result arrays once per target.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a fresh browser for whole-file retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch per retry, capped at two in PR CI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No rerun browser launched after the initial failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before reconciliation; grouped across all unique failed files.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload renderer and every unique file represented by the broad failure set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dynamic import per unique failed file, not per failed target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All whole-file tests complete before result reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Filter pass/failure arrays and repeatedly JSON-stringify title paths for each outstanding target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(T*(P+F)) result inspections and associated temporary allocations per recovering attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after browser completion and blocks retry scheduling or successful job completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T deduplicated outstanding targets (unbounded above 50), P passing tests, and F failures returned by the whole-file rerun. Boundary cardinality is grouped to unique failed files, but CPU reconciliation cardinality remains every target against every result.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One rerun at a time per browser; reconciliation is synchronous host CPU work after each attempt and cannot overlap the next attempt or job completion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no per-file or per-title-path index. `findPassedTargets` rebuilds filtered arrays, Sets, and JSON title-path strings independently for each target, so warm data does not reduce repeated scans.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence: the nested per-target filters and unbounded whole-file target map directly establish repeated CPU/allocation work on the critical path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of failure storms and exact suite cardinality are uncertain, but broad transient failures are realistic in a retry feature and the explicit >50 fallback proves target counts can exceed the bounded title-selection case.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated-work regression. Index passes and failures once by file and title path before resolving targets.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: An unattributed failure suppresses retries; debug mode forces maxReruns to zero and retains the browser for inspection. The runner reports the existing failure without launching another browser.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One browser launch; debug retained it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same initial execution boundary as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial module/CSS discovery and reporter output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One attempt's selected modules/tests; unattributed failure count affects only diagnostic formatting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same configured browser concurrency as before; no retry concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retry cache or additional attempt exists. Debug intentionally retains browser/server resources as pre-existing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from maxReruns and unattributed-failure branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for retry behavior; control flow explicitly disables additional attempts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff does not add expensive retry boundaries for these cases.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced normal successful browser CI, bounded targeted retries, whole-file fallback under broad failures, unattributed failures, debug mode, reporter output, browser/server cleanup, module loading, filesystem and HTTP boundaries, and local multi-browser concurrency. Submitted one repeated-work finding for unbounded target-by-result rescans during rerun reconciliation; other added costs are bounded or linear and do not meet the reporting threshold.
